cards.confidenceReason: PD-L1 ≥50% without EGFR/ALK supports guideline-preferred pembrolizumab. The choice between monotherapy and the chemo combination depends on disease burden and symptoms, which call for clinical judgement.

alternatives: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin + pemetrexed if burden is high or disease is progressing rapidly
Early-phase NCT05786924 or NCT06983743 are less suited to the first-line standard setting
Sotorasib or adagrasib are later-line, approved only after prior systemic therapy, so not first-line options here
cards.changesIf: Rapid clinical deterioration or a visceral crisis would favour the chemo-immunotherapy combination. Confirmed eligibility at an accessible site would favour trial enrolment.

boardSummary: Man in his 60s, former smoker (30 pack-years), ECOG 1, with newly diagnosed stage IVB lung adenocarcinoma (liver, left adrenal; brain MRI negative). He is symptomatic, with abdominal pain and weight loss. PD-L1 TPS is 60%. Tissue NGS shows KRAS G12C and TP53 R248Q. EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK and ERBB2 are negative, and STK11 and KEAP1 are wild-type. He is treatment-naive. The knowledge pack lists pembrolizumab monotherapy as preferred, and pembrolizumab with carboplatin and pemetrexed as an option for high or visceral burden. Sotorasib and adagrasib are later-line only. KRYSTAL-4 (NCT06875310), a first-line KRAS G12C trial, is recruiting. The trial-matcher's claim of South Asian sites is not verified by the evidence. He is on metformin, so baseline HbA1c and thyroid function are suggested before immunotherapy. Doses come from the dose calculator and require pharmacist and oncologist verification.
